The Constant at Which a Statically Started Filter Begins

Source: R/spec.R
static_filter_starts.Rd

Sets the property init_value of every modelterms7::gas() term written with init = "static" to the predictor of the model without the term, read at the first row of each group of the filter.

Usage

static_filter_starts(spec, split, data, weights, offsets, distrib, env, linpar)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

split

The equations, as statmod_equations() returns them.

data, weights, offsets, distrib, env, linpar

The arguments of statmod_spec(), with env the formula's environment.

Value

The specification, with the constant set on each such term.

Details

With init = "static" the first predictor of every group of the filter equals this constant whatever the parameters are, so the constant of the equation stays the level of the filter and does not double as its starting value. The model without the term is the same formula with each gas() call replaced by the development of its level (the right side of an omega ~ subformula) or, without one, by an intercept, so that the static model carries a level where the filter carries one. It is fitted once by statmod() with the same family, data, weights and offsets, and the constant of each group is its predictor of the parameter at the group's first row. With covariates the constant follows them: on the share of front-seat casualties in Seatbelts, share ~ law + gas(...) starts at the predictor of share ~ law at the first month, where the intercept-only fit would start it at the mean of the whole series and lose 2.07 in log-likelihood.

The fitted static model travels with the term as init_source, so a prediction that rebuilds the series on other rows reads the constants of its groups from the same model (static_filter_restart()).
